lines.en: Back in the golden room, where things were finally beginning to settle down...
: Attention, members of Class 1-A — Secret Santa will begin momentarily. Please retrieve your gifts and prepare to be disappointed if Sensei was assigned to you.
: AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAHHHHHH!
: Sorry, Miku.
: Is the megaphone really necessary, Touka?!
: Unfortunately, yes. My voice is too gentle and proper to penetrate the mass amount of Christmas joy circulating throughout the room.
: I’M GONNA PENETRATE YOU IF YOU DON’T TURN THAT DAMN THING OFF!
: Earbuds are available at the front of the room for anyone sensitive to noise. Thank you.
: Finished? Can I go back to having ears now?
: Are you not a musician? I was under the impression you were always exposed to loud noises.
: Just because I’m a musician doesn’t mean I’ve blown my ears out. That’s one of the few stereotypes attributed to us and it’s almost always totally untrue.
: Touka, what was that announcement? I couldn’t hear-
: Secret Santa will begin momentarily. Please retrieve your gifts and prepare to be disappointed if Sensei was assigned to you.
: Thank you!
: You’re not doing our kind any favors, Noriko! Take your bad hearing somewhere else!
: What?! Touka, can you hand the megaphone over to Otoha so I can hear what she just said?!
: She said you’re not doing musicians any favors to dismantle the offensive stereotypes that are apparently linked to you. This is news to me.
: THAT’S IT! PREPARE TO GET PENETRATED, HORSE GIRL!
: Security — please restrain this boisterous elf at once before my chastity is lost to another girl. Thank you.
: Somebody gimme a weapon! Ayane! Gun! Now!
: Hey, you have a weapon. Want to go test out your new crossbow on a few rich dudes?
: Heck no, I don’t! This thing ain’t fit for firing, Io! It’s gotta be from, like...the 1800’s or something! I’ve never even held a crossbow this old before!
: Okay. I guess Miku will just die then. Oh well. It was nice almost having two friends for a little while.
: Where the heck did Ayane even get this thing?
: Probably...the same weapons dealer she gets the rest of her stuff from? Is it really that impressive?
: Heck if I know! All I’m good for is shooting them. But this one feels more like a display piece.
: Well, where are you going to display it? Because our dorm room is starting to look like my aunt’s garage and I’m pretty sure we don’t have anywhere to put it.
: It’s not that bad, is it?
: You just lost Leonard for like a whole week because he was buried under a pile of clothes.
: Leonard can take care of himself. Plus, he likes the dark. Where’s your present though, Io?
: I don’t know. Maybe Sensei was supposed to get me something? Or his creepy niece? Or that green-eyed bimbo who’s always trying to be friends with me?
: Kirin? You guys would be nice together. Her eyes match your hair.
: Wow, you’re totally right. We would be great friends. I forgot about how important that shared connection is.
: Looks like I’ll just have to be your present then.
: Can I keep the wrapping paper on?
: Sure. I’ll be your doll for the entire year, so you can do whatever you want with me.
: I’ve only had one doll in my life and I took its head off like, immediately.
: But surely you wouldn’t do that to me, right?
: Riiiiiiight?
: Right?...
: Do you really think those puppy dog eyes work on me?
: Well, you’re right. Because they totally do.
: We’re not playing dress-up or any of that lame stuff, though. We’re learning glassblowing together.
: Yay! Me and Io get to blow something together that doesn’t make her want to puke!
: On second thought, maybe I’ll just go alone.
: Ahh, Christmas — the one day of the year where I can wait for people to give me gifts without being called rude.
: Yeah, it’s lots’a fun when Touka ain’t screaming into a megaphone. Plus, ya got that whole ramen thingy from Sana to spend the next week or two chowin’ down on.
: And what an excellent gift it is. It never ceases to amaze me how all of you can so easily figure out what I want most.
: Yeah! Same here! I usually don’t realize what I even want ‘til it’s in my hands, though.
: And...this year...
: This year what?
: Is that...toy...what you wanted the most?...
: You know it! I’ve gotta stretch out my girl parts so that I don’t wind up in the hospital. You’re small. You know how it is.
: That device is meant to be inserted inside of you?
: Yup! Just shove it in there every night before bed and you’ll be ready for a real wiener in no time at all! Like that whole thing about apples and doctors. A dildo each day keeps the damage away!
: Fascinating. I had no idea they were so dangerous.
: So is just...is just everyone open about this stuff all of a sudden?...
: What better time to start experimentin’ than the springtime of our youth? Especially when it actually is springtime for once.
: After a recent sexual experience with the ghost of Ami’s mother and watching the Emerald Guardian engage in virtual relations, I too am beginning to think more about such conduct.
: Can you repeat that first part please?
: No.
: You wanna give this baby a ride too, Sana? Feel free. Just make sure to wash it when you’re done.
: What?! No! I have...other methods! And you’re not supposed to share those!
: You’re not?
: This is news to me as well. But the sheer existence of such devices is news to me, so I am not sure if that says much.
: No! It’s unsanitary!
: Well, duh. That’s why I told you to wash it.
: It’s unsanitary even if you wash it, Miku!
: Oh.
: Okay. Well, definitely don’t tell Makoto I’ve been usin’ hers then.
: You’ve been what?!
: Nobody told me there were unwritten rules about this stuff, Sana! I’m figurin’ basically everything out myself, okay?!
: This is a common sense thing! Or...maybe it’s not! I don’t know! Either way, I’ve heard way too much about sex toys today! Just...be okay with having a small vagina! You don’t need to stretch it!
: You’re only sayin’ that cause you ain’t had a wiener in you yet! You don’t get it! I bet yours is even smaller than mine!
: If only there was some way we could compare!
: It appears that I will need to fuck both of you for the sake of preserving your friendship.
: You’d really do that for us?
: Christmas is all about bringing people together. But I must first acquire the penis.
: I was...thinking more someone like...you know...a boy.
: J-Just for...science, though. I need to...prove Miku wrong.
: Yeah. And I’ve gotta show Sana that there ain’t no way in a million hells she’s ready for major dong yet. Maybe like a little one, yeah. Major dong, though? She’d break in half.
: Do not fear, my companions. I will ask the Emerald Guardian where I can acquire major dong. She will know. She knows all of the sex things.
: E...Even if this is true...you won’t really be able to...feel us...Tsuneyo...
: Maybe we don’t need Tsuneyo at all if we just get a marker and measure how much we can-
: No, I think we need her. I just...you know...
: Second opinions are...important.
: My hunt for major dong begins now.
: Woo! Friendship!
: W...Woooo...
While things were going well in the golden room, there was somewhere else things weren’t going well.
It was somewhere far more special. With someone far more special currently inside.
She’d been sitting there for hours, hiding from her peers while gazing up at a tree that made her sick to her stomach for reasons she couldn’t properly describe or understand.
All the while, she’d been hoping she’d be found by a certain someone. Just like she’d hoped on Halloween before someone she didn’t want to find her did.
That was merely minutes before her new life was ruined — damaged to the point where, no matter what she did from now on, she would never be fully repaired.
Things like this happen to everyone at different stages in life.
But things like this don’t normally happen to everyone at different stages in different lives.
And that is what made Maya Makinami special.
It was less about “who she is” and more about the opportunities she’s had to change.
Yet, despite those countless opportunities, she’d always walked down the same path. Made the same choices. Followed the same footsteps she’d laid in prior timelines, prior chances.
Yet no one, not even I, knew how many it was. Or where those footsteps led to.
They always cut off before they reached the end of the trail.
: This is...for me?
: It’s a...present for the...Secret Santa event...
: Oh...right. I think I was...supposed to buy something for Io.
: I don’t know much about you, so...I hope you don’t mind that I asked the others for help.
: That shape...that size...I already know it’s a watermelon. I’m not in the mood to celebrate right now, though.
: Either way...thanks, I guess.
: You’re welcome.
: Is...everything okay?
: No? Yes? Whichever answer prevents you from ranting about how I just need to “find the light.”
: Touka says it’s best if I don’t always talk about the things I believe in.
: We can talk about you instead, if you like?
: May I...sit with you?
: Do whatever you want. It’s not like anyone else is coming.
: Is there someone in particular you want to come?
: Not really.
: It’s the teacher, isn’t it?
: Oh, okay. So does just everyone know that about me now or something? Were all those years of doing everything possible to keep it hidden worth absolutely nothing?
: I think it’s...more the fact that your feelings are so strong they can be seen plainly even without foresight.
: You have faced incredible challenges to preserve yourself, haven’t you?
: That’s one way to put it, I guess.
: Then, we’re the same in that regard.
: For a long time, I’ve been unsure of who I am when my most defining traits are stripped away. But things have been rather quiet lately...so I’ve had more time to think about it.
: I’ve been thinking — maybe I like spring better than the summer? The colors are nicer. The heat doesn’t make my uniform stick to my skin. And everything’s not flooded by the sound of cicadas.
: I still dream of ropes...and red threads that stretch across the city. But when I open my eyes in the morning, I don’t only see the color white anymore. I see everything.
: Or...maybe it’s less about “seeing” and more about what I imagine is there, hovering behind me — eternally intangible and unblemished by my perpetual impurity.
: Okay. You’ve lost me.
: If you could fit anything in that box...what would it be?
: It doesn’t have to be tangible. It doesn’t even have to be real. It can be anything you want.
: Is “love” too vague of an answer or can I stuff that in there and call it a day?
: Love from who? Of what type? There’s no box large enough to hold that word in its entirety.
: From who do you think?...What kind do you think?...
: You’ve all got me pegged already, don’t you? You know what I want. And it’s not something that could ever be put into a box.
: You say that now, but you don’t know what the future holds. And with the way you are now, you don’t know what the past held either.
: Oh, good. Am I gonna find out that you of all people remember the “old” me too?
: I’m...sorry for the passive-aggressiveness. I get that you’re...different from everyone else. I didn’t mean to say it like-
: I think she was afraid of me.
: I suppose I don’t blame her. People have always been afraid of me.
: You’re afraid of me now too. I can hear it. Feel it. But what no one ever understands is that I’m afraid as well.
: One difference between you and her, though...is that she’d have just walked away if I approached her like this.
: Maybe it’s because you haven’t seen me at the height of my clairvoyance yet? You’ve yet to witness my violently passionate thoughts about virgins and masturbation. You haven’t seen me as a worm.
: But I imagine seeing me as Yasu looks somewhat similar. Disgusting, but in a palatable manner. One that makes you pity me, not worried.
: I pitied her, though.
: Not because she believed with her whole heart that she knew what was happening...but that there was so much pain inside of her that she’d stopped even feeling it.
: Right now, what you are experiencing would have been all but unfathomable to her. But long before then, it would have been commonplace.
: You’ve yet to be anesthetized by time and the actions you take in an effort to combat it. And the invisible blood of every clock in the world has returned to its rightful hands rather than yours.
: That’s why they shake so much now. That’s why you’re afraid.
: You don’t realize where we are.
: And...you do?
: Sometimes, I think so.
: Others...I think I’m just supposed to think that.
: There are details unclear to even me...and they fade as the days go by as the voice that once carried them in has decried my worth and all I am. All I was. All I’ll be.
: But even when these eyes are gouged from their sockets, I’ll be able to see that all of this is temporary...
: That there’s somewhere else we’ll go when we’re no longer needed here. Somewhere bigger. Somewhere better.
: Somewhere she wanted to go that you haven’t decided exists yet.
: This world...
: There’s something...seriously wrong with it...
: Isn’t there?...
: Yes.
: But even Heaven has its problems, Maya. If you believe in a place like that...
: There’s something wrong with every world.
: But maybe there’s one perfect for you?
: And maybe we’ll meet again there one day.
: Maybe when we do, you won’t be afraid of me anymore.
: I’m not afraid of you, Yasu.
: Your heart beats faster when you lie. Does it excite you? Or do you just feel guilty?
: Okay. Maybe I’m a little afraid of you. But still...I think you can be kind of...sweet too. Apparently.
: Hm...no change in pace.
: I think you’re sweet too, Maya.
: I can’t wait to see you at your ripest.
